patch_description: The Steiner-tree multicast approach achieved the best cost (759.09) by deduplicating shared transfers, while the PathOracle/TreeCostModel approach contributed the idea of marginal-cost greedy assignment with a shared-edge accounting model. The crossover builds the Steiner tree once (as in the best program), then refines it with the shared-edge greedy: for each destination we consider the tree path plus up to k alternative shortest simple paths, and select the one with the lowest marginal cost given edges already committed (used edges are free). Destinations are processed in order of tree-path cost so the cheapest, most-shareable routes commit first. Each partition reuses the final per-destination routes, keeping shared edges transferred only once while allowing a destination to take a cheap alternate path when it beats its tree path. This preserves the exact BroadCastTopology API and output format.
